fixed.before: 34.3 gives a variant for the preceding 'mound of Denpu'; rnp,yt may be 'fresh plants' or 'years'. 35.2: Busiris (Djedu) has a restored final [j]; ṯz-pẖr 'and the reverse' marks that the address may be read both ways (Busiris says it to Shu); ḫnm 'unite with' may also be 'nurse'.
fixed.after: 34.3 gives a variant for the preceding 'mound of Denpu'; rnp,yt may be 'fresh plants' or 'years'. 35.2: Busiris (Djedu) has a restored final [j], with which the word may instead be Djedwy, 'the Two Djed-pillars'; ṯz-pẖr 'and the reverse' marks that the address may be read both ways (Busiris says it to Shu); ḫnm 'unite with' may also be 'nurse'.

fixed.before: Spell for not letting a man's corpse perish in the necropolis, to rescue him from the eating of the *bas* (souls) that are imprisoned in the Duat, and for not letting his wrongs on earth be raised up against him, for keeping his flesh and his bones sound against worms(?) and every god who does harm in the necropolis, for letting him go out and come down as he wishes, and do everything in his heart without being hindered.
fixed.after: Spell for not letting a man's corpse perish in the necropolis, to rescue him from the Eater of *bas* (souls) who is imprisoned in the Duat, and for not letting his wrongs on earth be raised up against him, for keeping his flesh and his bones sound against worms(?) and every god who does harm in the necropolis, for letting him go out and come down as he wishes, and do everything in his heart without being hindered.

fixed.before: 163.2: wnm bꜣ.pl, 'the eating of bas', may mean being eaten by them; dnm, here 'worms', is uncertain. Irheb, Herty, Remen, Senhaqereg and Senhaperegen are unidentified, foreign-sounding names. 163.5: zꜣ 'protection' or 'son'. 163.7: dp 'taste', perhaps 'consume'.
fixed.after: 163.2: wnm bꜣ.pl is 'the Eater of bas', a demon (n,tj 'who' is singular); dnm, here 'worms', is uncertain. Irheb, Herty, Remen, Senhaqereg and Senhaperegen are unidentified, foreign-sounding names. 163.5: zꜣ 'protection' or 'son'. 163.7: dp 'taste', perhaps 'consume'.

not_upheld.e2#2: The note already gives the alternative: ꜥḥꜥj 'may be a time of day'.
not_upheld.e2#3: sqd.w,t with its feminine ending is 'voyage', not the masculine sqd.w 'crew'; sdgꜣ,wt is marked obscure in the note.
not_upheld.e2#4: ꜥfd.t is marked uncertain in the translation and the note; 'four' is no surer a reading.
not_upheld.e2#5: 'A prisoner who is in the prison, whose punishment has been decreed' is a standard reading of Khufu's order; the objection's imperative is an alternative, not a correction.
not_upheld.e1#1: n ṯwt js is 'for you are', the usual reading of this spell ('for you are the Sole Star at the shoulder of Nut'), not the negative n ... js.
not_upheld.e4#1: rdj ... m can be 'give forth from': 'he makes him vomit [what is] in his heart' gives that sense; the objection's 'into' is not the only reading.
not_upheld.e4#2: bkꜣ 'morning, tomorrow' is a standard reading ('I am Yesterday and Tomorrow'), as in Nu's version of the same spell; the note gives it.
not_upheld.e4#4: psn (pzn) is a kind of bread in the lexicon, as the note says; 'a large portion of meat' renders wr n jwf.
not_upheld.e6#8: n,tj tw j:m=f has tw, 'I': 'this evil state that I am in' is the writer's, as the letter's complaint requires; the objection's 'in which you are' contradicts the pronoun.
